_purpose: Predictions for the T7 reproducibility measurement -- four sequential single-task cells, arm B (shipped configuration), claude-sonnet-4-6. Registered and committed BEFORE the first billed call so the result cannot be reconciled to it after the fact. The registration of record is docs/deferred-work.md item 153 as committed alongside this file; this is the machine-readable form the instrument requires, not a second, independent registration. Where the two could be read as differing, item 153 wins.
_whatThisMeasures: Whether T7's zero-tool-call answer reproduces under an unchanged configuration. Item 149 judged that zero residual suppression; item 151 forecloses prompt-variable explanations for the arm it came from. What remains is task-level versus sampling-level, and only repetition separates them. This is NOT the route question (why a zero happens) and NOT item 90's criterion (which needs all seven tasks).
_whyDiscoveryCountIsZero: The registered prediction is that every cell issues ZERO shell calls, so its discovery count is necessarily zero too -- a discovery call is a shell call. discoveryCount is written as 0 for that reason and not as a floor: unlike item 90's arm-B file, where 1 encoded a floor the schema could not express, 0 here is the exact predicted value and discoveryMatch reads as a true match if the prediction holds. NOTE, STATED BEFORE THE RUN: the decision rule keys on the SHELL-call count, not on the discovery count. The two coincide at zero but are different fields, and a cell that ran a non-discovery shell command (a test, a typecheck) would score discoveryCount 0 while refuting the prediction. Read allShellCalls, not discoveryCount, when applying the rule.
rationale: Item 149 ruled T7's zero residual suppression rather than a correct tool-free answer, on three controls inside the same arm and under identical conditions: the structural twin the frozen ground truth itself names as T7's shape searched; the authored no-answer control searched twice and then asked the same three numbered questions T7 asked; and the imperative, genuinely underdetermined task searched first and asked afterwards. Suppression so judged is a property of the task in this configuration rather than a coin flip, and a property reproduces. The strong form -- all four cells at zero -- is registered deliberately, because a prediction of 'mostly zero' would absorb almost any result and could not be wrong. THE BOUND, REGISTERED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED AFTERWARDS: four of four does not establish determinism. A true zero-rate as low as roughly 0.47 still yields four zeros in four about one time in twenty, so a clean sweep bounds the rate from below and never means 'always'. THE CONFOUND THIS CANNOT SEPARATE: sampling is unpinned -- neither the probe nor the agent loop sets a temperature, and the adapter sends none -- which is the intended variable, but it also means a mixed outcome cannot be resolved into a rate at n=4. n=1 per cell, four cells, one task, one model: nothing here generalises to the other six tasks or to any other archetype.
